results.title: US hikes tariffs to further isolate China from its EV supply chain ambitions
results.content:
Starting this year the US is increasing the tariff rate on lithium ion batteries and battery parts to 25% from 7.5% earlier. For non-electric vehicle lithium ion batteries a tariff of 25% will be introduced in 2026.

The move will likely lead to the US having even greater reliance on South Korean and Japanese manufacturers to plug its supply chain gap. [...] However, the US accounted for less than 1% of China’s EV exports last year.

#### Why has natural graphite been added to the list of tariffs?

Beginning in 2026 the US will apply a tariff of 25% on Chinese natural graphite imports, amove aimed at reining in China’s near-monopoly in the graphite used for making batteries for electric vehicles and shows that it intends to diversify anode supplies away from China. [...] #### What other critical raw materials are set to join the tariff list?

The Biden administration has also proposed the inclusion of “certain critical materials” to the tariff list, which is yet to be finalised. Tariffs of 25% will be introduced starting this year for certain critical minerals.

#### What are the implications for the rare earth to permanent magnet supply chain?

Permanent magnets will draw a tariff of 25% from 2026 onwards.

results.title: Which Tariffs Could Affect Your Next Car?
results.content:
Over the next two years, automakers will be able to apply for an import adjustment offset on tariffs paid for foreign components of U.S.-assembled vehicles. These offsets are limited to 3.75% of a car’s final MSRP on tariffs paid between April 3, 2025, and April 30, 2026; the maximum offset amount drops to 2.5% of a car’s final MSRP for tariffs paid between May 1, 2026, and April 30, 2027. The offset will be discontinued thereafter. The order claims this offset equals up to 15% of a [...] Image 20: electric cars with the longest range 2025 Polestar 3 jpg2025 Polestar 3 | Manufacturer image
## China

China has been a particular focus in U.S. trade restrictions in recent history, with the previous Biden administration implementing stiff 100% import duties on Chinese electric and plug-in hybrid cars alongside additional tariffs on other components related to electrified vehicles and green energy. [...] Related:High Interest Rates, Fewer Used Cars Make Affordability the Toughest Challenge of 2025

Tariffs are taxes applied to imported goods that are paid by the party who imports them. You can check out our previous coverage for a more detailed explanation, but in short, this means that automotive companies — most of whom have highly international supply chains — will have to pay extra for vehicles or vehicular components they import from outside the U.S.

results.title: How Tariffs Could Affect EV Prices | Toyota of Denton
results.content:
A tariff is a tax placed on imported goods. In 2025, the U.S. government
implemented new tariffs that directly impact the automotive industry. These
tariffs apply to:

Vehicles imported from countries without favorable trade
agreements

Automotive components, particularly EV batteries, semiconductors, and
electronic control modules [...] You’re interested in upcoming bZ Series models.

You’re watching for new EV incentives.

You want access to refreshed 2026 hybrid trims.

But there’s also risk:

Future tariffs could further increase pricing, ruining your
plan. 

Inventory for newer models may remain limited. 

Government incentives may change or expire. 

## FAQs: Tariffs and Toyota EVs

### Q: Will tariffs raise the price of the Toyota bZ4X? [...] Electric vehicles (EVs) often rely on global supply chains. When tariffs
increase, production costs can rise significantly, especially for EVs that
depend on non-domestic battery packs or advanced electronics.

## How Tariffs May Influence EV Prices

You may see price increases in areas such as:

Base Manufacturer’s Suggested Retail Price (MSRP)

Trims that include high-end technology packages

Battery-electric models built with internationally sourced parts
